page: Google Cloud Platform a3-edgegpu-8g-nolssd is an accelerator-optimized server instance featuring eight NVIDIA H100 GPUs from the Hopper architecture, delivering a total of 637 GB of VRAM. The host system is powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor with 208 vCPUs (104 physical cores) running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 1872.0 GB of system memory, providing 9.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include any local SSD storage, requiring external storage solutions for persistent data.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates top-tier performance in multi-core CPU execution, memory bandwidth, and specialized cryptographic operations. The multi-core stress-ng and Passmark CPU tests place this server in the top 10% of benchmarked systems, aided by advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks also ranks in the top 10%. For LLM inference, the platform achieves top-tier prompt processing speeds, reaching 5430.06 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

The primary tradeoff of the a3-edgegpu-8g-nolssd is the complete absence of local SSD storage, which necessitates network-attached storage and may impact workloads requiring high-speed local scratch space. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server represents a highly consolidated, dense resource profile designed to maximize GPU-to-CPU throughput, reducing the need for multi-node clustering for moderately sized models. It is structured for workloads such as large language model training and inference, ray tracing, multi-threaded decompression, and high-throughput data processing.
